results.title: Digital levers for sustainability: a meta-analytic review of ...
results.content: Some studies report strong positive links between DT and ESG, especially when digital investment fuels green innovation, supports evidence-based decisions, or enhances disclosure quality (Ding et al., Citation2024; Wu, Citation2024). To clarify these effects, DT is categorized into five typologies: (i) General DT maturity (e.g. digital orientation, IT investment intensity) (Pham et al., Citation2024), (ii) AI and intelligent systems (e.g. predictive analytics, robotics) (Al Halbusi et al., Citation2025), (iii) Data and Infrastructure (e.g. big data platforms, cloud systems), (iv) Business Process Digitization (e.g. ERP, workflow automation) (Wang & Zhang, Citation2024), and (v) Innovation Capabilities (e.g. smart product development, digital R&D) (Khan et al., Citation2023). Dynamic-Capabilities research shows that sectors built around rapid innovation, e.g. ICT and platform services, reconfigure digital tools faster than heavy manufacturing or multi-sector conglomerates, magnifying DT’s ESG impact (Kong et al., Citation2024; Luo, Citation2024). These results reinforce Fu and Li (Citation2023) moderation findings: AI improves ESG performance only in firms with high digital maturity and strong internal controls.
